title: Purely inseparable smooth proper curve maps are relative Frobenius
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-pc-field-characteristic]. Let $X,Y$ be smooth proper integral $k$-curves of dimension one [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a nonconstant $k$-morphism, where nonconstant means not factoring through a $k$-rational point of $Y$. Assume that the induced extension $k(X)/f^*k(Y)$ of function fields is finite purely inseparable [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-pc-field-tower]. Then there are a unique integer $n\geq0$ and a unique $k$-isomorphism $h:X^{(p^n)}\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ such that $f=h\circ F_{X/k,n}$. Here
$$X^{(p^n)}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_n)}\operatorname{Spec}k,\qquad \varphi_n(a)=a^{p^n},$$
with structure morphism the second projection [def-pc-base-change]. The relative Frobenius $F_{X/k,n}:X\to X^{(p^n)}$ is the morphism defined by the pair consisting of the $n$-fold absolute Frobenius on $X$ and its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Absolute Frobenius [def-weil-absolute-frobenius-scheme] is the identity on points and raises local sections to their $p$th powers; for $n=0$ the canonical identification $X^{(1)}\cong X$ makes $F_{X/k,0}$ the identity.

source.place: Tag 0CCZ (curves-lemma-purely-inseparable-smooth), restricted to algebraically closed k and smooth target; the n-fold relative Frobenius is varieties.tex Tag 0CCG (varieties-remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), including n=0 by the identity convention.

proof.text: Put $L=k(X)$ and $E=f^*k(Y)\subseteq L$. By [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms], these are finitely generated fields of transcendence degree one over $k$, with the given compatible $k$-inclusions. Apply [lem-sfb-one-variable-purely-inseparable-subfield] to the assumed finite purely inseparable extension $L/E$. Obtain $r\geq0$ with $[L:E]=p^r$ and $E=L^{p^r}$.

source.place: Tags 0CCX (lemma-purely-inseparable) and 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), field-theoretic content of their proofs, specialized to algebraically closed k: degree-p tower and equality with the power subfield.

proof.text: Put $T=X^{(p^r)}$ and $F=F_{X/k,r}$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-relative-frobenius-degree], $T$ is a smooth proper integral dimension-one curve and $F$ is nonconstant. By [lem-sfb-relative-frobenius-function-field-image], $F^*k(T)=L^{p^r}=E=f^*k(Y)$. Thus $\theta=(F^*)^{-1}\circ f^*:k(Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(T)$ is a $k$-isomorphism, where the inverse is taken on the common image.

source.place: Tag 0CCG (remark-n-fold-relative-frobenius), defining projection formula, and curves.tex Tag 0CCY (lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), identification of the Frobenius image field with kK^p; over algebraically closed k use the affine power calculation, for all n including n=0.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms], $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$ induce nonconstant $k$-morphisms $h:T\to Y$ and $h^{\prime}:Y\to T$. Their composites induce the identity field maps, so injectivity of that correspondence gives $h^{\prime}h=\operatorname{id}_T$ and $hh^{\prime}=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Finally $(h\circ F)^*=F^*\theta=f^*$, and the same injectivity gives $f=h\circ F$. This also covers $r=0$, with the canonical identity-base-change identification.

source.place: Tag 0CCY (curves-lemma-inseparable-deg-p-smooth), passage from equal function subfields to a unique curve isomorphism by Tag 0BY1; iterated in Tag 0CCZ.

proof.text: If $f=g\circ F_{X/k,m}$ for a $k$-isomorphism $g:X^{(p^m)}\to Y$ and an integer $m\geq0$, then [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms] says $g^*$ is an isomorphism and $f^*=F_{X/k,m}^*g^*$. Consequently [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-relative-frobenius-degree] gives $p^r=[L:E]=p^m$. Since $p\geq2$, the sequence $p^n$ is strictly increasing, so $m=r$. With this exponent fixed, $F^*h^*=f^*=F^*g^*$ and injectivity of the field embedding $F^*$ give $h^*=g^*$. Injectivity in [lem-sfb-proper-curve-function-field-morphisms] now gives $h=g$.

source.place: Tag 0CCZ (curves-lemma-purely-inseparable-smooth), uniqueness of exponent and isomorphism; degree of relative Frobenius from varieties.tex Tags 0CCF and 0CCG.

The function-field map is pinned by the generic-point square (Spec K(Y) -> Y is a monomorphism), with Module.Finite and IsPurelyInseparable checked on it.
